title: Derived singleton evaluation below and above the input level
statement:
For m≤n, derived evaluation at m of the singleton derived left extension from n is canonically derived tensor along B_n→B_m, intertwining actual Hom transposes with the original derived transition. For m>n its evaluated value is zero for every derived input object.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J)) (T : SystemTensorCoherence S)
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n)
theorem systemSingleDerivedAbove (m n : ℕ) (hm : n < m)
    (P : DerivedCategory (systemLevel B n)) :
    IsZero ((derivedSystemEvaluation B m).obj
      ((systemSingleDerivedExtension B n S T).derived.obj P))
```

proof.text: The ordinary below-level tensor comparison and actual transition satisfy the unit-mate identity. Apply the general normalized evaluation-mate theorem with identity source evaluation and the flat-term K-flat resolving class. For vanishing, choose such a representative of the input; its ordinary singleton extension is zero at every term above n. The derived comparison and exact evaluation factorization identify evaluation with localization of this zero complex.
